release_rule: No entry below 'reviewed' may be shown to a participant. Fill 'missing' with a first-language reviewer, then raise each status.
warning: Every entry here came out of OCR on a scanned page and NONE of it is confirmed. Treat this file as a reading of a photograph, not as a dictionary. Nothing may reach a participant until a first-language reviewer has checked each glyph against the printed book and raised the status.
notes: The source PDF carries no text layer, so the pages were rasterised at 200 dpi and read with tesseract. The dictionary prints four to six columns per page, which the reader frequently interleaves: a line can end in a word from the next column. Every entry above was checked for that, but an unnoticed splice is still possible.
The printed format is ENGLISH/otjiherero followed by the noun-class plural marker in brackets, e.g. 'CHILD/omuatje (ovan-)'. Those markers are reproduced in the notes, not in the target string.

Several ids that the OCR did not reach are left in 'missing' rather than guessed: consent sentences, risk, benefit, ethics, interpreter, signature, photograph, complaint, voluntary, 'you can stop at any time'.
Otjiherero is a Bantu language with noun classes and with tone that the dictionary does not mark; a single-word gloss cannot be dropped into a sentence unchanged.

t.no.note: OCR: 'NO/kako, ayee'. 'Ayee kako' = no, not at all. Read by OCR from the scanned page; the glyphs must be checked against the printed dictionary before use.

t.consent.note: OCR gives 'PERMISSION/omeriindjikirs' with the tail garbled; the standard form is omeriindjikirira. Must be confirmed on the printed page, and 'permission' is not the same legal idea as 'consent'.
